title: Deduplicate a Sorted Linked List
summary: Remove repeated values from a sorted linked list in place and return its head.
statement: The linked list is sorted in nondecreasing order, so equal values are adjacent. Rewire next pointers so that one node remains for each distinct value, and return the original head. Do not create a replacement list.
constraints: The list is sorted in nondecreasing order.
The input may be an empty linked list.
hints: Sorting makes duplicate nodes adjacent, so one pointer can remove repeats without extra storage.
Compare each node with its successor; bypass equal successors and advance only after the next value changes.
Pseudocode checkpoint: identify the state, update it once per step, and return only after the deduplicate_sorted_linked_list invariant is complete.
Editorial: Compare each node with its successor; bypass equal successors and advance only after the next value changes. The intended bounds are O(n) time and O(1) space.
